title: KV vacuuming metapool and fragmentation suppression plan
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Propose and implement a metapool-based KV allocation strategy plus a cooperative "vacuuming" process to suppress fragmentation on GPU-resident KV caches. The goal is to preserve low tail latency under continuous batching while reducing memory waste from long-tail fragment accumulation.

Background: Our current KV cache uses a single global pool with LRU-style eviction and opportunistic compaction. Over long uptimes, small variable-length entries produced by different models and sequence lengths create many holes that are expensive to compact synchronously. Continuous batching amplifies the issue: larger batch windows increase transient KV insert/delete churn and increase allocation churn for KV slices, causing higher fragmentation and occasional OOM-eviction storms on heavily-utilized GPUs. Existing approaches in the codebase (slab coalescers, slot anchoring, background compaction) have reduced symptoms but we still see: 1) 8-15% memory headroom loss on 80%+ sustained load nodes, 2) compaction runs causing CPU/GPU stalls when run impulsively, and 3) degradation in P95 token latency during compaction spikes.

Goals:
- Reduce long-term fragmentation ratio by >= 30% on replicas running high-churn workloads.
- Keep compaction/vacuum work off the critical path (no compaction-induced P95 token latency regressions).
- Ensure continuous batching throughput improvements remain intact (no throughput regression > 5%).
- Provide telemetry and knobs for ops to tune vacuum aggressiveness per pool and per tenant.

Design proposal: metapool + vacuuming + age-bins
1) Metapool concept: split GPU KV memory into a small-number of independent "metapools" (fixed-size arenas) based on size classes and volatility. Example lanes: Tiny (<=128 bytes), Small (129-1K), Medium (1K-8K), Large (>8K), and Ephemeral (short-lived entries from recent batches). Each metapool uses a simple free-list allocator tuned to its size class to avoid internal fragmentation and to bound search cost.

2) Age-tiered placement: on allocation, attempt to place entries into a lane using a combination of requested capacity and predicted lifetime (inferred from request attributes: model id, sequence length, prompt type). We will add a lightweight predictor (heuristic table initially: e.g., chat prefix entries go to Ephemeral) and refine offline. This reduces mixing long- and short-lived objects that create holes.

3) Cooperative GPU vacuuming: introduce a low-priority background vacuum that runs on GPU compute streams reserved for async housekeeping. Vacuum tasks:
   - Coalesce adjacent free blocks within a metapool by updating chunk metadata (no copies) where indirection is available.
   - For variable-length entries that can't be coalesced in-place, opportunistically move cold entries into compacted pages during idle windows using low-priority CUDA kernels and async memcpy; update pointer indirections atomically.
   - Reclaim fully-empty pages back to a global free page pool so we can shrink ephemeral lanes under pressure.
Vacuuming is rate-limited by a shared token bucket per GPU and backed off when tail latency signals rise.

4) Idleness hooks and batch-aware scheduling: vacuum tasks should run during model idle windows and between batching cycles. Integrate with the continuous batching scheduler to expose short (5-50ms) windows for micro-vacuum passes. Also add a per-tenant soft-reserve that prevents vacuum from starving active workloads.

5) Migration-friendly soft-reserve and pinned-inflight heuristics: maintain a small soft-reserve to avoid eviction thrashing for large VT caches during live migration/rollouts. Mark entries referenced by in-flight requests as pinned for short TTL; vacuum respects pins.

6) Telemetry and knobs: add metrics per metapool: allocated_bytes, free_bytes, fragmentation_ratio (1 - largest_contiguous / total_free), vacuum_time_ms, vacuum_throughput_bytes, pinned_bytes, compaction_migrations, and eviction_pressure. Expose runtime knobs: vacuum_rate_bytes_per_sec, idle_window_threshold_ms, metapool_size_class_cutoffs, predictor_weights.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Spike (weeks 0-1): implement in-memory metapool scaffolding (allocation/free API) + unit tests; synthetic benchmark harness to exercise mixed size churn.
- Prototype vacuum (weeks 2-3): low-priority GPU kernel + async move path; integrate with batching scheduler idle hook; simple heuristic predictor.
- Canary (week 4): enable on a small fleet of dedicated nodes behind feature flag. Add telemetry dashboards.
- Iterate (weeks 5-7): tune size cutoffs, vacuum rate, predictor; add eviction fallback and graceful disable path.
- Rollout (week 8+): staged rollout to Dedicated pool, then Private; add ops runbook.

Acceptance criteria:
- Synthetic mixed-workload benchmarks show >= 30% drop in fragmentation_ratio compared to baseline after 24h run at 85% GPU memory utilization.
- No P95 token latency regression in continuous-batching end-to-end test (<5% change).
- Vacuum_time_ms stays bounded and visible in telemetry; vacuum_rate can be tuned without restarts.
- Rollout runbook documented with toggles and safe-disable procedure.

Risks & mitigation:
- Moving cold entries on GPU could introduce pointer races. Mitigate via atomic double-buffered indirection table updates and epoch-based reclamation.
- Vacuum kernels may contend with model kernels when scheduling is tight. Use CUDA stream priorities and token-bucket rate limiting; early abort if kernel launch latency starts trending up.
- Predictor misclassification may place long-lived items into ephemeral lane; add fast migration path and conservative defaults.

Rollout & experiment plan:
- Start with internal canary on non-customer Dedicated nodes running mixed chat + embedding workloads.
- Run 48h stability tests with continuous workload and automatic comparison of fragmentation_ratio, eviction_count, and latency.
- If successful, gate enabling by model family and tenant risk level; run A/B for 2 weeks with traffic split.

Operational runbook (outline):
- Feature flag: runtime.kv.metapool.vacuum.enabled (per-node).
- Emergency disable: set vacuum_rate_bytes_per_sec=0 and drain vacuum queues; if persistent, disable feature flag and restart runtime.
- Dashboards: fragmentation_ratio (per node, per tenant), vacuum_time_ms, eviction_pressure, pinned_bytes.

Links & artifacts: will attach benchmark harness repo, design doc (Confluence), and initial PRs here when available.
